The post RhPf Electronics Reveals the Shodhana Overdrive appeared first on Pedal Haven.
item.content:encoded:
RhPf Electronics has released Shodhana, a balanced overdrive designed to move fluidly between two distinct gain characters: a transparent MOSFET boost and a focused, high-mid forward drive. Rather than stacking gain stages or adding tone controls, Shodhana’s single Drive knob lets both gain and voicing evolve together, allowing players to shape not just how much distortion they hear, but how the tone sits in the mix.

At low Drive settings, Shodhana behaves like a fast, full-range boost, adding clarity and energy without altering the natural character of the guitar and amp. As the Drive increases, the response gradually shifts toward a stronger upper-mid bite and faster attack, delivering the kind of snap and presence that helps single notes and chords cut clearly through dense arrangements. The transition is continuous, making it easy to find anything from subtle enhancement to assertive, mix-ready drive.

Shodhana is designed to reward interaction with the instrument. As the high-mid snap builds with gain, the guitar’s tone control becomes a powerful way to fine-tune how much edge and bite you want in the sound. Rolled back, the pedal delivers smoother textures; wide open, it delivers maximum attack and cut. Whether used as a wide-open boost or a focused drive, Shodhana responds clearly to touch, pickup choice, and real-time playing dynamics.

Key Features

  • Dual-path gain architecture with parallel MOSFET boost and overdrive circuits
  • Single Drive control that adjusts both gain and voicing without a separate tone knob
  • High-mid focused response that develops strong bite and fast attack as gain increases
  • High headroom and wide output range for boosting, stacking, or clean dynamic use
  • Minimal two-knob layout with Drive and Level controls only

Street price is $179 USD. Shodhana is available at select retailers and directly from the RhPf Electronics online store at rhpfelectronics.com.

Like all RhPf Electronics products, Shodhana is not a clone, mod, or derivative circuit. It is a fully original design developed from the ground up.

RhPf Electronics is a guitar effects company based in Basel, Switzerland, designing fully original circuits with a focus on musical feel, clarity, and long-term reliability.

item.content:encoded:
This post may contain affiliate links

Klowra Pedals, in collaboration with Hotone, has just launched the Mantra, a beautifully designed dual expression pedal that allows you to externally control two parameters at the same time – whether that is on two different pedals, or digital amps, MIDI controllers, or anything else that accepts expression pedals.

Where to Buy the Mantra

View Price on Amazon

 

The Mantra features two separate ¼” TRS output jacks that can each be plugged into separate devices, allowing you to control each expression parameter simultaneously. 

 

The pedal comes with one ¼” TRS cable, which is a nice addition. But if you need a second one, these are the TRS cables I’ve been using.

 

Each of the TRS output jacks on the Mantra has its own Direction (-/+) switch that allows you to reverse the polarity of that specific jack, granting you more control over the expression control.

  • (+) Mode: Toe-down increases the value.
  • (-) Mode: Toe-down decreases the value.

 

Despite being so feature-packed, the Mantra is relatively small and won’t take up a ton of space on your pedalboard.

Where to Buy the Mantra

View Price on Amazon

 

The Mantra is housed in a rugged, metal enclosure that features an extremely cool, originally hand-drawn silk screen artwork on the top of the expression treadle. The treadle is also topped with a coarse, sandpaper-like material (like skateboard griptape) for added grip when using the pedal.

 

Lastly, the Mantra is a passive pedal, meaning it doesn’t need any power to be used.

 

Tech Specs:
Power: Passive; No power required

Dimension: 2.0″H x 6.4″D x 3.2″W

Weight: 0.98lbs

Outputs: 2x 1/4″ TRS jacks, 10kQ, Linear

 

The Klowra team was kind enough to send a Mantra to me to check out, and I have been really enjoying integrating it into my pedalboard. The expression curve is very smooth, and having the ability to control the expression inputs on two different pedals on my board has been really fun!

 

Learn more about the Mantra here: https://www.klowra.com/mantra-dual-expression-pedal

You can buy the Mantra on Amazon here (affiliate link)

item.title: Klowra Pedals Vein Pitch Shifter Pedal Review
item.dc:creator: pedalhaven
item.description:
This post may contain affiliate links The Klowra Pedals Vein reignited my love for pitch-shifting effects. I’ve always had a bit of a love-hate relationship with pitch shifter pedals. On one hand, they are extremely fun to have on your pedalboard, but on the other hand, dealing with latency issues has always made it hard […]

The post Klowra Pedals Vein Pitch Shifter Pedal Review appeared first on Pedal Haven.
item.content:encoded:
This post may contain affiliate links

The Klowra Pedals Vein reignited my love for pitch-shifting effects.

I’ve always had a bit of a love-hate relationship with pitch shifter pedals. On one hand, they are extremely fun to have on your pedalboard, but on the other hand, dealing with latency issues has always made it hard to find one that is truly usable. 

Enter the Vein Pitch Shifter from Klowra Pedals. I’ve been diving into this pedal for the past couple of weeks, and it has been a mind-bending experience in the best way. It has rekindled my desire to add a pitch shifter to my pedalboard.

 

Note: If you already have a Vein Pitch Shifter (or are thinking of buying one), make sure you have it updated to the latest firmware update (2.0.2). This update significantly improves the pedal’s response time and fixes latency issues. Seriously, it’s like a night-and-day difference between the old firmware version and the new one.

What is the Vein Pitch Shifter?

As it sounds, it’s a pitch-shifting pedal, but under the surface, it offers far more than that (we will get into that later). The Vein is a polyphonic pitch shifter that offers 17 different pitch intervals, ranging from two full octaves up/down to strange, microtonal sounds.

Where to Buy the Vein Pitch Shifter

View Price on Amazon

 

Here is a breakdown of the 17 pitch intervals you can choose on the Pitch Select knob:

  •  (-)②: Up (or Down) 24 Semitones
  •  (-)①: Up (or Down) 12 Semitones
  •  (-)p5: Up (or Down) 7 Semitones
  •  (-)p4: Up (or Down) 5 Semitones
  •  (-)M3: Up (or Down) 4 Semitones
  •  (-)m3: Up (or Down) 3 Semitones
  •  (-)M2: Up (or Down) 2 Semitones
  •  (-)m2: Up (or Down) 1 Semitone
  •  UNI: Unison

As you can see, you get a lot of choices with each mode (except for UNI), each having the option to pitch up or down – giving you access to all kinds of cool octave sounds and interesting harmonies. The Unison (UNI) mode acts more like a chorus pedal effect that you can adjust using the Rate and Detune knobs.

I’ve really been enjoying the 12 and 24 semitone settings, as these provide either one or two full octaves up or down. Some of the other intervals sound quite good for creating interesting harmonizing sounds, and some intervals (like 1 or 2 semitones) are honestly a bit… strange – but if you’re into eerie, microtonal sounds, then you will dig those settings too!

As I mentioned above, the UNI mode is also extremely usable. It is like a chorus effect and sounds fantastic.

Where to Buy the Vein Pitch Shifter

View Price on Amazon

The other controls on the front of the pedal are what set the Vein apart, as they introduce a ton of interesting, creative features. Let’s talk about them:

LED Button:

The LED on the front of the pedal not only indicates whether the effect is on or off, but it is also a button that allows you to perform various functions and access hidden/secondary features of other knobs:

    • Latched/Momentary mode: Press the LED button to change between Latched or Momentary mode when the pedal is engaged.
    • Save a “Snap-Set”: Press and hold the LED button to save the current parameter settings, which you can later recall.
    • Secondary Knob Functions: Press and hold the LED while adjusting a knob to adjust the secondary functions of the knobs (see more below).
    • Access Negative Pitch Intervals: Press and hold while turning the Pitch Select knob to access negative interval pitches and lower octaves.
  • Rate: This knob adjusts the LFO’s pitch modulation frequency.
  • Tone: (Rate Knob Secondary Function): Adjusts the high frequencies of the wet signal.
  • Detune: Adjusts the stereo deviation of the LFO’s microtonal pitch changes (up to 100 cents).
  • Mix: Controls the wet/dry mix of the effect and your input signal.

Vein’s Glide feature:

The Vein features a Glide function where the pitch will ramp up (or down) to the desired pitch when the pedal is activated – the Glide feature can be engaged in both Latched and Momentary modes.

  • Glide ATK: Controls the attack time (how long it takes to ramp to the desired pitch)of the Glide feature.
  • Glide RLS: Controls the release of the glide effect when the pedal is deactivated.

Vein’s Ramp feature:

The Vein also has a Ramp function that fades the effect back and forth between the panel-set (current knob configuration) and a saved ‘Snap-Set’. The Ramp feature can also be used in both Latched and Momentary modes, and can be tweaked using the secondary functions of the Detune and Mix knobs.

  • RampATK (Secondary function of Detune knob): Controls the attack speed of the Ramp effect.
  • RampRLS (Secondary function of the Mix knob): Controls the release speed of the Ramp effect.

This has quickly become my favorite feature of the Vein. Having the ability to fade between two different settings on the pedal is really cool. I was jamming on the UNI setting and using the Ramp feature to jump to the +1 Octave pitch setting for fun little accents before ramping back down to the UNI setting.

External Controls

Where to Buy the Vein Pitch Shifter

View Price on Amazon

I’ve found that the Vein becomes even more fun and usable when paired with an expression pedal, which effectively turns the pedal into a pseudo-Whammy type of pedal. An external expression pedal allows you to externally control the pedal’s Ramp or Glide features – giving you the ability to easily change between the “Panel-Set” settings and the “Snap-Set” you’ve saved.

The setup is extremely easy to do. Just connect your expression pedal to the Vein’s “CTRL” input jack using a 1/4″ TRS cable (like this one). The Vein’s LED will then blink red, and you can calibrate the expression settings by cycling through the full range of your expression pedal so the pedal recognizes the expression pedal’s output – and then it’s ready to go.

 

Final Thoughts

Klowra Pedals have created something really special, and honestly, extremely fun with the Vein. Their new software update fixed a lot of latency issues that I experienced when I first got the pedal (before it was updated), but after the update, it has become an incredibly versatile and powerful pitch-shifting pedal that is packed with so many cool, usable, and unique features.

If you’re on the hunt for a new pitch shifter, the Vein is one that should certainly be on your radar!

Learn more about the Vein here: ​​https://www.klowra.com/vein-pitch-shifter

You can buy the Vein on Amazon here (affiliate link)

item.title: This Pedal Company Designed a Pedal to Raise Awareness for a Rare Disease. Meet RhPf Electronics’s ‘Tri-Hormonic Phalanx’ Boost/Overdrive Pedal

item.description:

RhPF Electronics has released the Tri-Hormonic Phalanx, and it’s what they’re calling a ‘precision tone enhancer’ that allows you to add gain to hand-picked high, mid, and low frequencies separately – allowing you to dial in […]

The post This Pedal Company Designed a Pedal to Raise Awareness for a Rare Disease. Meet RhPf Electronics’s ‘Tri-Hormonic Phalanx’ Boost/Overdrive Pedal appeared first on Pedal Haven.
item.content:encoded:
This post may contain affiliate links

This extremely unique boost pedal gives you complete control over your gain structure.

RhPF Electronics has released the Tri-Hormonic Phalanx, and it’s what they’re calling a ‘precision tone enhancer’ that allows you to add gain to hand-picked high, mid, and low frequencies separately – allowing you to dial in every aspect of your tone exactly as you want it.

On the surface, it’s a boost pedal, but it is far more exciting than that. The Tri-Hormonic Phalanx works by separating your signal into three parallel paths, each running through its own MOFSET gain stage and its own level control. You can then decide to add gain to just your mids or highs, for example, or keep a frequency band clean to maintain clarity or create unique drive sounds. Then you can use the independent volume controls for each frequency to ensure the output is well-balanced in the mix.

Key Features:

  • Triple-Band Parallel Architecture
  • Independent Gain and Level controls for Low, Mid, and High Frequencies
  • MOFSET Gain Stages for Natural, Amp-like Harmonic Character
  • Full-Range Clean Boost or Targeted Drive for Specific Frequency Registers

The Tri-Hormonic Phalanx is a powerful addition to the front of your pedal chain and can work well as an extremely unique and powerful boost or drive pedal on its own. Alternatively, it can be used in front of other overdrive or fuzz pedals to really shape which frequencies are being pushed into them.

Check it out at the RhPf Electronics website here.

The Story Behind the Tri-Hormonic Phalanx

The Phalanx carries a subtle tribute to Acromegaly into its identity. Acromegaly is a rare disease, and early diagnosis can drastically improve patients’ lives. Your awareness can make a difference.

Thomas from RhPf Electronics writes:

“In late 2023, I received a diagnosis of acromegaly. This rare condition transformed my life, pushing me to reevaluate my priorities. Although I decided to continue my corporate job, I also chose to pursue a lifelong dream: sharing my passion for creating high-quality guitar pedals. For years, I designed pedals for myself, family, and friends. However, this journey inspired me to make my work available to others.

The Tri-Hormonic Phalanx represents the beginning of this new chapter. Its name reflects its unique tri-band parallel distortion design and my battle with acromegaly. I named the three gain controls—IGF-1 (Low), GH (Mid), and ACTH (High)—after key hormones affected by this condition. IGF-1 (Insulin-like Growth Factor 1) and GH (Growth Hormone) are closely tied to the overproduction that causes acromegaly. Meanwhile, ACTH (Adrenocorticotropic Hormone) highlights another critical pituitary function. These labels honor my journey and help raise awareness of this rare condition.

The Tri-Hormonic Phalanx blends my passion for music and design with a cause close to my heart. It’s more than just a pedal—it’s a testament to resilience, creativity, and the power of pursuing dreams despite life’s challenges.”

 

About RhPf Electronics

RhPf Electronics is a family-run pedal company from Basel, Switzerland. The team focuses on original circuits built with intention, musical purpose, and Swiss precision. Every pedal is hand-built, voiced carefully, and designed to help players get more out of their rigs.

Learn More about RhPf Electronics here: https://rhpfelectronics.com/

The pedal originated in plugin form as the SilverBOY TSM-AI amp, a virtual […]

The post A Guitar Pedal Inspired by a Plugin? The SilverBOY Preamp Brings a Digital Amp to the Physical World appeared first on Pedal Haven.
item.content:encoded:
This post may contain affiliate links

In a world where analog guitar amps and effects are being digitally modeled and recreated as computer programs, Dirty Boy is fighting back by releasing the SilverBOY, the first preamp pedal inspired by a digital plugin.

The pedal originated in plugin form as the SilverBOY TSM-AI amp, a virtual amplifier created in collaboration with Two notes Audio Engineering for their GENOME platform. That digital amp captured the spirit of the original Dirty Boy Preamp.

The plugin sounded so good that the Dirty Boy team felt it needed to exist in hardware form, and the SilverBOY was born.

‘SilverBOY was born as code. Now it exists as hardware. It’s the first time we’ve built an analog circuit from a virtual amp — reversing the whole industry’s direction,’ said Danny Gomez, Dirty Boy owner. 

They worked backwards, capturing the feel, responsiveness, and sound of the virtual TSM-AI amp to shape the tone of the SilverBOY, then rebuilt it in physical form.

What is the SilverBOY?

The SilverBOY is a fully analog amp simulator made for direct LINE use, a highly-tweakable preamp for your amp’s FX loop, or a tube-like boost to drive the front end of your amp – capable of producing anything from sparkly cleans to snarling, collapsing fuzz-soak saturation.

The pedal is housed in a gnarly-looking enclosure with a DIY feel. The front of the pedal is completely packed with knobs to dial in your tone, including everything from Volume and Drive to a 3-band EQ section and a knob for the Variac Simulator, which emulates amp sag and creates voltage-starved fuzz sounds.

As far as jacks go, the SilverBOY offers an input jack, a stereo LINE IN jack with a level control, a headphone jack, a PREAMP output, and an Emulated output.

The SilverBOY also features a built-in 2×12 cabinet emulation.

 

Head over to the Dirty Boy website to learn more about the SilverBOY.

The post Orange Amps Launches “King Comp” Compressor Pedal appeared first on Pedal Haven.
item.content:encoded:
(22nd October, 2025 – London, UK) – The new Orange Amps King Comp is a super low noise Class A VCA compressor pedal with 18V DC power supply for extra headroom and subtle envelope shaping control. It brings studio-style compression dynamics to any pedalboard and offers a warm musical response with an exceptionally low noise floor.
Developed to meet the ever-evolving musical needs of guitarists and bassists, the King Comp pedal enhances sound by adding sustain, snap, and sparkle rather than flattening it, offering smooth, musical, pro-level compression with real character.

The super useful dual attack and release knobs mean users can set how quickly the compression kicks in and shape every note they play. The versatile attack control allows anything from understated tightening to pronounced pogoing bounce to be dialled in. At the same time, the equally adaptable release control gives long-lasting sustain for notes and chords that can go on for miles. Plus, there is also visual feedback of any compression applied when the King Comp’s onboard LED switches from blue to pink.

At the heart of the King Comp pedal is the Class A VCA compression circuit that delivers precision dynamics with a warm, natural feel.  There is also a high-quality buffered bypass to ensure signals stay strong and consistent, even when the pedal is off. The buffer maintains clarity, keeping sound punchy and defined, and makes the King Comp reliable as an always-on part of any setup.

Running with the external 18V DC supply maximises the King Comp’s dynamic range and reduces compression artefacts, so the pedal delivers the most transparent version of any instrument’s tone, making it especially useful with hot pickups, basses, and more complex pedalboards.

The King Comp pedal offers precise dynamic control with a musical feel that responds like a great amp. To find out more please go to www.orangeamps.com.

The post Orange Amps Launches “King Comp” Compressor Pedal appeared first on Pedal Haven.

The Twin Peaks Eiger-Mönch isn’t just yet another delay. With two purpose-voiced delay lines that can run in parallel or interact in a true cascade, it redefines what a delay pedal can be: a source of rhythm, texture, and inspiration that stays musical at every setting. RhPf Electronics just released the Twin Peaks Eiger-Mönch, a […]

The post RhPf Electronics Unveils the Twin Peaks Eiger-Mönch, Dual Delay appeared first on Pedal Haven.
item.content:encoded:
The Twin Peaks Eiger-Mönch isn’t just yet another delay. With two purpose-voiced delay lines that can run in parallel or interact in a true cascade, it redefines what a delay pedal can be: a source of rhythm, texture, and inspiration that stays musical at every setting.

RhPf Electronics just released the Twin Peaks Eiger-Mönch, a two-voice delay that opens doors to new creative spaces. One channel is shimmery and airy, the other mellow and warm. Each line has its own Speed and Feedback control. In parallel mode, the voices spread wide and clear, giving a stereo-like dimension from a mono rig. In cascade mode, the two lines feed into each other, weaving syncopated swing and evolving echoes that answer each other while fading out.

What makes it different:

  • Two distinct voices: vintage warmth on one side, modern brilliance on the other. Each has independent controls for endless rhythmic combinations.
  • Parallel mode: wide, layered echoes that stay open and defined; a stereo-like sense of space.
  • Cascade mode: true cross-feedback so each line feeds the other; repeats intertwine and evolve into living textures while fading out.

The Twin Peaks Eiger-Mönch is no ordinary delay pedal or one-trick pony. It creates ambience and textures ranging from subtle reverb to intricate rhythm patterns that groove. Every setting stays musical thanks to carefully tuned feedback, avoiding runaway oscillation and gimmicks.

Rather than sitting on top of your tone, it becomes part of it. Elevating riffs, chords, and textures without getting in the way. Guitarists keep coming back to one thing: it sparks creativity.

“We wanted a fresh take on delay, one that inspires patterns and syncopation without relying on glitchy tricks. It should sound good anywhere on the knobs and feel like part of your sound. We wanted a delay that lands on a board and stays there.”

Learn more about the Twin Peaks Eiger-Mönch on the RhPf Electronics site.

Like every RhPf pedal, the Twin Peaks Eiger-Mönch is a ground-up original, not a clone, not a mod. Hand-built in Basel by a small family-run workshop, it reflects a dedication to sound, detail, and originality.

item.content:encoded:
Utrecht-based boutique guitar pedal builder Dronechov Noise Machines announced
Megaphone, a transparent, high-impedance MOSFET boost pedal.

 

 

Megaphone carries the sound, feeling, and clarity of tube boosters and can drive your preamp into distorted bliss. The pedal offers extra headroom and doesn’t color your tone, but is packed with enough output to saturate any amp. Compatible with both Single Coil and Humbucker pickups, Megaphone sounds impressive not only when used on a guitar but on bass as well.

While boosting itself keeps the signal clean, the pedal’s three-band EQ allows you to add the right amount of punch along the spectrum. This makes it extremely versatile and handy, no matter if you’re playing 1970s rock or high-gain metal. At first glance, Megaphone is a simple boost pedal, which it can be, but plug it directly into the Return input of an amp, and you can even use it as a preamp.

You can learn more about the Megaphone and order it here.

 

About Dronechov Noise Machines

Dronechov Noise Machines is a one-man operation, founded in 2020. It started as a passion project for building various mods and pedal clones, but in early 2025, they introduced their own Black Philip fuzz. The first limited batch quickly sold out, but a new one is already available. Megaphone is their second guitar pedal, which like all of their items, is hand-built in Utrecht, the Netherlands.

The Mosferatwo, originally designed for grungy blues-rock guitarists, is an overdrive pedal that features a 100% unique circuit utilizing two different gain stages to deliver a wide range of drive sounds, from clean boost to the sound of a full-blown […]

The post RhPf Electronics Reveal The Mosferatwo, Dual Stage MOFSET Overdrive appeared first on Pedal Haven.
item.content:encoded:
RhPf Electronics, out of Basel, Switzerland, have revealed their new MOSFET-based overdrive pedal, the Mosferatwo.

The Mosferatwo, originally designed for grungy blues-rock guitarists, is an overdrive pedal that features a 100% unique circuit utilizing two different gain stages to deliver a wide range of drive sounds, from clean boost to the sound of a full-blown tube amp being pushed to the max – all while remaining extremely responsive.

Shop Pedal Haven Merch

The Mosferatwo features some interesting controls that offer a variety of unique ways to shape your tone:

  • Drive knob: controls both gain stages, allowing you to dial in the desired amount of distortion.
  • Focus knob: Changes the dynamic feel and frequency response of the drive sound, from bold and bloomy to tight and articulate.
  • Heart and Bite Toggle Switches/Knobs: These allow you to boost carefully-selected low and midrange sections of your EQ, further shaping your tone. The small black knobs above them allow you to dial in which frequencies are boosted.

“Its saturated yet articulate tone, dry crunch, and melodic grit have resonated with those chasing anything from jangly garage textures to hypnotic, riff-heavy drive. The pedal now finds itself at home across genres — from vintage blues to modern desert rock and everything in between.”

 

Head over to the RhPf Electronics website to learn more about the Mosferatwo or watch the demos available – including an extremely cool interactive demo from Loopy Demos and a tool that lets you tweak the knobs of the Mosferato to see exactly how it’s shaping your tone.

item.content:encoded:
This post may contain affiliate links

 

J. Rockett Audio Designs, the pedal company behind one of the most iconic Klon clones, The Archer, just released their latest pedal – the Archer Select.

Since its release in 1994, the Klon Centaur, and its now-astronomical price tag, has sparked a world of different Klon clones. And with those clones comes debate – a lot of which is centered around which clipping diodes make the best ‘Klon’ sound.

 

The J. Rockett Audio Designs team has decided to put that question to rest with the release of the Archer Select – which features seven different clipping modes (6 NOS germanium diodes plus a red LED clipping option).

WHERE TO BUY

See Price Amazon

Review and Overview of the Archer Select

The J. Rockett Audio Designs team has taken the classic Klon formula and turned it into something truly special and customizable, with the Archer Select. It really nails that classic Klon sound, but it invites you to explore the circuit in new ways by changing the clipping diodes – which provide a wide range of new overdrive sounds that you don’t find in many other Klon clones.

The Archer Select retains everything that made their original Archer pedals great, but adds a lot of little bonuses (like the DI Output with a built-in speaker simulator) that make it a great choice for the studio or the stage.

Archer Select’s Features

The Archer Select features a “Clipping” footswitch, which allows you to select one of the 6 additional clipping modes you’ve selected on the “Clipping” knob. When the “Clipping” footswitch is not engaged, the Archer Select uses OA10 diodes. 

 

The other 6 clipping diode options on the “Clipping” knob are:

  • 1N270 NOS germanium diodes (The same diodes found in the original Archer)
  • 1N695 NOS germanium diodes (The same diodes found in the Jeff Mod Archer)
  • 1N34A NOS germanium diodes (The same diodes found in the original Klon Centaur)
  • D9B NOS germanium diodes 
  • D9E NOS germanium diodes (The same diodes found in the Archer iKon)
  • Red LEDs

Although the differences between all of these clipping modes are quite subtle at low-to-medium gain settings, you start to hear how these clipping modes affect the compression and mid-range frequencies once you get into the higher gain settings.

Aside from the clipping options, the Archer Select features all the knobs you would expect on a k-style overdrive pedal – Output (volume), Gain, and Treble (Controls the high end).

If the clipping options aren’t enough, the J. Rockett team has also implemented a 1/4″ D.I. output on the side of the pedal equipped with an onboard speaker simulator for monitoring and/or direct-in recording. The toggle switch on the front of the Archer Select is a ground lift for the D.I. output.

 

 

Overall, the Archer Select is an incredibly versatile drive pedal that delivers that sweet Klon-like tone right out of the box. The addition of the various clipping options makes it seem right at home for any pedalboard or studio setup.
